questions.q: Why does this lesson say 'everyone should just follow good practices' is not a real governance model?
options: Because good practices are never actually correct
Because it doesn't name who owns what or give that ownership actual authority, and hope doesn't survive four independent teams moving at their own pace
Because Salesforce requires a written governance document by policy
Because business units are legally prohibited from having their own standards
questions.explain: A real governance model names specific ownership with actual authority; a general intention toward good practices has no enforcement mechanism against four independently-moving teams, which is exactly why Risk #6 was rated high likelihood.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four things LTV Global's Architecture Center of Excellence (CoE) owns, per this lesson?
options: The shared data model
Coding and declarative standards
The Change Advisory Board process
Day-to-day execution of every business unit's individual feature development
questions.explain: The CoE owns the shared data model, coding/declarative standards, the CAB process, and architecture decision records — but deliberately does NOT own day-to-day execution, which stays distributed to each BU's own admins and developers.

questions.q: How does LTV Global's CoE avoid becoming a bottleneck, given it governs four independent business units?
options: By personally reviewing and approving every single change across all four BUs
By owning standards centrally while leaving execution distributed — only changes touching shared/cross-BU territory route through the CAB process
By disbanding whenever a BU disagrees with a standard
By requiring every BU to use the exact same metadata with no local variation at all
questions.explain: The CoE practices centralized ownership of standards without centralized execution, consistent with Lesson 19's split — BU-specific changes with no shared dependency don't need full CAB review.

questions.q: How does this lesson's governance model resolve Risk #6 from the Chapter 1 risk register?
options: By ignoring the risk, since governance sprawl was never a real concern
By naming a specific body (the CoE), specific ownership, and a specific process, rather than a general intention to be more coordinated
By eliminating all four business units and merging them into one
By removing the Change Advisory Board entirely
questions.explain: Risk #6 (governance sprawl) is resolved with a concrete, named mechanism — the CoE's ownership structure and CAB process — rather than a vague commitment to coordination.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect the CoE back to Lesson 5's target-state vision?
options: It contradicts the vision's governance commitment
It gives evidence for the vision's 'sustainable governance' commitment, since standards and decisions are owned by a standing body with BU representation, not by any single individual's memory
The CoE has no connection to the vision statement at all
It replaces the vision statement with a new one
questions.explain: The vision promised governance that survives one engagement team member leaving; because the CoE's standards and decision records are owned collectively, not by one person's memory, this design can point to actual evidence for that commitment.
